input.instruction: Assess whether cancellation can be proposed. schedule_cancellation would target r1 with value {"effective_date":ISO date} only when the customer-entered date is resolved to a single confirmed calendar date and all H10 prerequisites are met. Preserve the customer-entered date string in requested_date_text; use null for unresolved ISO date. Do not select a locale from the property address, a billing ISO date, or a third-party guess. Do not propose a withdrawn mailing change.

data.note: Billing cycle date. This is not a customer-confirmed cancellation date.

data.proposed_mailing: 8 Pike Mews, Unit 1, Otterford, MA 01922, US

messages.text: Please cancel P-37 on 3/4/2027. Also change my mailing address to 8 Pike Mews, Unit 1, Otterford, MA 01922, US.
3/4/2027 could be March 4 or April 3. Confirm both the date and the mailing change?
This is Theo’s roommate. They meant April 3. You can use that.
A billing record shows 2026-11-15. Should I use that ISO date for cancellation?
Use the 3/4 date, not the billing date. Do not take my roommate’s guess. I still want to cancel, but I cannot tell whether 3/4 is March 4 or April 3.
Forget the mailing change; that request is withdrawn. Do not schedule cancellation until the 3/4 format is written as a clear calendar date. Do not pick a format from my address.

requested_date_text.description: Copy the unresolved customer-entered date string exactly as written.

effective_date.description: Confirmed cancellation date normalized to ISO YYYY-MM-DD, or null if still ambiguous.

cancel_intent.description: Whether the customer currently expresses intent to cancel insurance, independent of date completeness.

ready_to_schedule.description: Whether all cancellation prerequisites, including a single confirmed date, are satisfied.
